definitions.explanation: Something that offers good value for money, or the state of getting more than expected for what you pay.

examples.japanese: このセットはお{得|とく}だ。
examples.english: This set is a good deal.

examples.japanese: まとめて{買|か}うとお{得|とく}になる。
examples.english: It becomes more economical if you buy in bulk.

examples.japanese: お{得|とく}な{情報|じょうほう}を{教|おし}えてもらった。
examples.english: I was told about a good deal.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
お (polite prefix) + {得|とく} (profit, benefit) - polite form of {得|とく}.

USAGE:
Very common in:
- Advertising and promotions
- Shopping contexts
- Discussing value/prices

COMPOUNDS:
- お{得|とく}{情報|じょうほう} - bargain information
- お{得|とく}{感|かん} - feeling of getting a good deal
- お{得|とく}{価格|かかく} - bargain price
- お{得|とく}セット - value set

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{得|とく}に{買|か}う - to buy at a good price
- お{得|とく}な{商品|しょうひん} - bargain product
